sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in South Carolina?
sections.html:
Property tax in South Carolina is run locally. The Department of Revenue says it is administered and collected by local governments with assistance from the department, and about two-thirds of county-levied property taxes support public education (SCDOR property tax page). Your county assessor values the house, the auditor and treasurer handle the bill, and school and city levies ride on the same notice.

That means rules in this guide come from the state code, while rates, office hours and payment options come from your county. Call the county treasurer before you finalize a sale date.

sections.h2: What assessment ratios does South Carolina use?
sections.html:
The state taxes a percentage of fair market value, and the percentage depends on use. The ratios below come from SC Code 12-43-220.

PropertyRatioSection
Owner-occupied legal residence, up to five contiguous acres4%12-43-220(c)
Other real property not otherwise provided for6%12-43-220(e)
Agricultural real property, qualifying individuals and partnerships4%12-43-220(d)(1)
Manufacturing and utility property10.5%12-43-220(a)(1)

A rental house or second home falls under the 6% line, so owner-occupants and investors see different bills on similar values.

sections.h2: How often are South Carolina properties reappraised?
sections.html:
Each county must appraise and equalize property once every fifth year (12-43-217). Valuation is to be complete by the end of December of the fourth year, with taxpayers notified of value or classification changes of $1,000 or more. New values are assessed in the fifth year.

A county may postpone putting revised values into effect by ordinance, for no more than one property tax year. If you plan to sell, find out which year your county is in. A reassessment year can move the bill your buyer inherits.

sections.h2: When is the bill due and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Taxes are due between September 30 and January 15 after assessment (SC Code 12-45-70). Penalties begin after the later of January 16 or 30 days after notices are mailed (12-45-180(A)).

If unpaid byPenalty added
The January deadline3%
Before the second day of the next FebruaryAdditional 7%
Before the seventeenth day of the next MarchAdditional 5%
Still unpaid in MarchTreasurer issues a tax execution, plus costs

A county may allow installment payments by ordinance. Taxpayers elect in writing between December 1 and January 15, and five installments of 16 2/3% fall on February 15, April 15, June 15, August 15 and October 15 (12-45-75). Taxes paid through escrow are excluded.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a South Carolina assessment?
sections.html:
Start with written notice of objection to the assessor within 90 days after the assessor mails the assessment notice (SC Code 12-60-2510). In years with no notice, an appeal may be made in writing at any time. One filed before the first penalty date applies to that tax year; one filed after applies to the next.

  1. Notice of objection to the assessor, or a written request to meet, within the 90 days.
  2. Conference with the assessor, scheduled within 30 days of the request or as soon after as practical (12-60-2520).
  3. Written protest within 30 days after the conference.
  4. Appeal to the county board of assessment appeals within 30 days after the assessor's response (12-60-2530).
  5. Contested case hearing before the Administrative Law Court within 30 days after the board's written decision (12-60-2540).

If an appeal is still open on December 31 of the tax year, the assessment is adjusted to 80% of the protested amount for payment purposes, with interest settled afterward (12-60-2550).

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the age 65 homestead exemption?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption removes the first $50,000 of fair market value of the dwelling for owners who are 65 by December 31, or who are disabled or legally blind, and have lived in the state at least a year (SC Code 12-37-250). It applies to county, municipal, school and special assessment real estate taxes. The application deadline is before July 16 of the tax year.

Our separate homestead page goes deeper. For sellers, the point is simple: a buyer who is not eligible will not carry the same exemption.

sections.h2: What happens to the 4% rate when you sell?
sections.html:
The 4% legal residence rate does not transfer automatically. The owner must apply before the first penalty date for the first year claimed, and when ownership changes the former owner must notify the assessor within six months while the new owner files a new application (12-43-220(c)(2)(vi)). Failing to notify or losing eligibility can bring a penalty of 100% of the tax paid plus interest at one-half of one percent per month (12-43-220(c)(2)(vii)(A)).

So a buyer who plans to live in the house should file promptly. A buyer who rents it out will be on the 6% ratio.

sections.h2: What if taxes go unpaid and the county sells the property?
sections.html:
Delinquent notices go out on April 1 or as soon after as practicable, and property is advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks (SC Code 12-51-40). The sale is a public auction, and the winning bidder pays in full that day.

The defaulting taxpayer, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within twelve months of the sale (12-51-90). Interest on the bid is 3% in months one to three, 6% in months four to six, 9% in months seven to nine and 12% in months ten to twelve. Notice is mailed neither more than 45 days nor less than 20 days before the redemption period ends (12-51-120).

sections.h2: How is tax handled when a house sells mid-year?
sections.html:
If property changes hands after assessment, the new owner may apply before a tax execution sale, and the auditor estimates the share of tax owed on the portion acquired (12-45-140). Paying that share discharges the property from those taxes. Penalties must be waived when a house transferred mid-year, the notice went to the prior owner and the new owner got no timely notice (12-45-180(B)).

Closing agents normally settle the year's tax at the table. Tell your closing attorney about any unpaid prior-year bills so they show on the payoff list. A cash buyer can often close with back taxes owing, because the payoff comes out of proceeds.

sections.h2: What exemptions help sellers who build or flip houses?
sections.html:
South Carolina exempts 100% of the improvement value of newly constructed detached single-family homes offered for sale, for the period set out in 12-37-220(B)(51). The statute also exempts the first $10,000 of net depreciated value of business personal property for small businesses (12-37-220(B)(54)).

These exemptions are narrow and carry conditions. An investor who is rehabbing instead of building new should not assume the new-construction exemption applies. The county auditor can tell you.

sections.h2: Why does the county treasurer only collect certain bills?
sections.html:
County treasurers are prohibited from collecting any tax except what has first been entered on the tax duplicates of their county, or what the auditor has ordered (12-45-60). In practice, the bill your closing agent pulls will match the duplicate, and nothing outside it can be demanded at the table.

City or town taxes get the same relief as county taxes when a new owner pays a proportionate share (12-45-170). If land moves from one county to another by annexation, taxes are prorated between the two counties for that year (12-45-390).

sections.h2: What happens to the sale if the county takes the property?
sections.html:
On redemption, the officer cancels the sale in the tax sale book, and the purchaser is notified by mail to return the receipt for a refund of the price plus interest (12-51-100). After a tax deed is issued, the delinquent tax collector notifies the defaulting taxpayer and the owner of record of any excess due (12-51-60).

That excess is money left after taxes, penalties and costs. An owner who thinks a sale is coming should call the county delinquent tax office early. Selling before the auction avoids the twelve-month clock entirely.

faqs.q: When are South Carolina property taxes due?
faqs.a: Between September 30 and January 15 after assessment. Penalties start after the later of January 16 or 30 days after notices are mailed, beginning at 3% (SC Code 12-45-70, 12-45-180).

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my property assessment?
faqs.a: 90 days after the assessor mails the assessment notice. In years without a notice you may appeal in writing at any time (12-60-2510).

faqs.q: Do I pay while an appeal is pending?
faqs.a: Yes. If the appeal is unresolved on December 31, the assessment is adjusted to 80% of the protested amount for payment, with a correction and interest afterward (12-60-2550).

faqs.q: Can I sell a house with back property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, the unpaid tax and penalties are typically paid from sale proceeds at closing. Ask the county treasurer for a current payoff figure.

faqs.q: How long can a delinquent tax sale be redeemed?
faqs.a: Twelve months from the sale date, with interest on the bid that steps up from 3% to 12% (12-51-90).
